message.content:
Read-only investigation for Nxeon (VPS/hosting platform, staging tree /opt/nxeon-staging). No code changes — report back only.

Context: the owner is reviewing a sent cold-email campaign in the admin panel (`/admin/coldemail/sent`) — one example shown is subject "quick one, Avenue Right", segment "Local Businesses — Shared Hosting (Variant A)", body ends with "Worth a look before your next renewal?" and a plain "— Nxeon Team" signoff, no logo, CAN-SPAM footer with real postal address + unsubscribe link. The email is getting good opens (tracked, "opened ×2" etc. shown in the admin list) but has **no clickable CTA link** anywhere in the body pointing the recipient anywhere.

Find and read the actual cold-email system:
1. The email template/generation code — search for "coldemail" across `lib/`, `app/admin/`, `worker/` (likely something like `lib/coldemail.ts`, `lib/cold-email-templates.ts`, or similar) to find where the body text ("Hey — noticed [business]'s site... Worth a look before your next renewal?") is generated/templated, and whether it's a per-segment template (the "Variant A" naming suggests there are multiple template variants).
2. Determine whether the system currently supports ANY kind of link in the email body at all (even an unsubscribe-style plain link) — check the actual HTML/text generation to see if inserting a URL is straightforward or if there's some reason it was omitted (e.g., a deliverability concern about link-heavy cold email, or simply an oversight).
3. Check if click-tracking exists anywhere in this system (separate from the open-tracking already visible in the admin UI) — search for "click" tracking, redirect/wrapper URLs, or UTM parameter handling related to cold email specifically.
4. Identify what a good link TARGET would be for the "Local Businesses — Shared Hosting" segment specifically — check if `/web-hosting` (the real live shared-hosting page, recently redesigned) is the natural target, or if there's a more specific landing page/promo already built for this exact segment (check for anything cold-email-specific like a dedicated landing page or promo code tied to this campaign).
5. Check how many other template variants exist for this and other segments (to understand if a link needs to be added to just this one template or many).

Report back (under 400 words): where the template lives, whether adding a link is a simple change or has a technical/deliverability reason it's currently absent, what click-tracking (if any) exists, the best real landing-page target for this segment, and how many templates would need the same fix.

1	// Cold Email Engine — tracking-event persistence (open pixel + click redirect).
2	//
3	// Shared by app/api/coldemail/track/open/[token] and .../click/[token]. Both
4	// routes serve an unauthenticated GET straight to a recipient's mail client, so
5	// every write here is best-effort and never throws — a DB hiccup must never turn
6	// into a broken pixel or a failed redirect.
7	//
8	// Three things happen per event:
9	//   1. an immutable EmailEvent(OPEN|CLICK) row — the per-event history that
10	//      lib/coldemail/engagement.ts already reads for the campaign "who engaged"
11	//      table (app/admin/coldemail/campaigns/[id]).
12	//   2. denormalized openedAt/openCount (clickedAt/clickCount) on the ColdSend row
13	//      itself — the same shape as EmailLog's tracking columns (see
14	//      manual-migration-emaillog-tracking.sql / manual-migration-coldsend-
15	//      tracking.sql), for cheap per-send lookups without joining EmailEvent.
16	//   3. a DeliverabilityEvent row. THIS WAS THE MISSING PIECE: the pixel/redirect
17	//      routes previously wrote only the EmailEvent, but
18	//      worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts's rollup sweep aggregates MetricsDaily
19	//      exclusively from DeliverabilityEvent (see EVENT_TO_COUNT in that file,
20	//      which already had OPEN/CLICK mapped — it just never received any). Without
21	//      this write, every open/click tile on the admin analytics page
22	//      (app/admin/coldemail/analytics) would stay at 0% forever even with real
23	//      engagement happening.

25	import { db } from "@/lib/db";
26	
27	async function loadSendContext(sendId: string) {
28	  return db.coldSend.findUnique({
29	    where: { id: sendId },
30	    select: {
31	      id: true,
32	      campaignId: true,
33	      contactId: true,
34	      inboxId: true,
35	      inbox: { select: { sendingDomainId: true } },
36	    },
37	  });
38	}
39	
40	/** Record one OPEN for `sendId`. Returns false (no-op) if the send doesn't exist. */
41	export async function recordOpenEvent(sendId: string): Promise<boolean> {
42	  const send = await loadSendContext(sendId).catch(() => null);
43	  if (!send) return false;
44	
45	  await db.emailEvent.create({ data: { sendId, type: "OPEN" } }).catch(() => null);
46	
47	  // openCount always increments; openedAt only stamps on the FIRST open (a raw
48	  // increment has no "only if null" form) — same two-call pattern as EmailLog's
49	  // /api/track/email/[id]/open route.
50	  await db.coldSend
51	    .update({ where: { id: sendId }, data: { openCount: { increment: 1 } } })
52	    .catch(() => null);
53	  await db.coldSend
54	    .updateMany({ where: { id: sendId, openedAt: null }, data: { openedAt: new Date() } })
55	    .catch(() => null);
56	
57	  await db.deliverabilityEvent
58	    .create({
59	      data: {
60	        type: "OPEN",
61	        inboxId: send.inboxId ?? null,
62	        sendingDomainId: send.inbox?.sendingDomainId ?? null,
63	        campaignId: send.campaignId,
64	        contactId: send.contactId,
65	        sendId: send.id,
66	      },
67	    })
68	    .catch(() => null);
69	  return true;
70	}
71	
72	/** Record one CLICK for `sendId` to `url`. Returns false (no-op) if the send doesn't exist. */
73	export async function recordClickEvent(sendId: string, url: string): Promise<boolean> {
74	  const send = await loadSendContext(sendId).catch(() => null);
75	  if (!send) return false;
76	
77	  const meta = url.slice(0, 300);
78	  await db.emailEvent.create({ data: { sendId, type: "CLICK", meta } }).catch(() => null);
79	
80	  await db.coldSend
81	    .update({ where: { id: sendId }, data: { clickCount: { increment: 1 } } })
82	    .catch(() => null);
83	  await db.coldSend
84	    .updateMany({ where: { id: sendId, clickedAt: null }, data: { clickedAt: new Date() } })
85	    .catch(() => null);
86	
87	  await db.deliverabilityEvent
88	    .create({
89	      data: {
90	        type: "CLICK",
91	        inboxId: send.inboxId ?? null,
92	        sendingDomainId: send.inbox?.sendingDomainId ?? null,
93	        campaignId: send.campaignId,
94	        contactId: send.contactId,
95	        sendId: send.id,
96	        meta,
97	      },
98	    })
99	    .catch(() => null);
100	  return true;
101	}

content.text:
## Findings: Cold-Email Click Link Investigation

**Where the copy lives:** There are two layers. `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/coldemail/templates.ts` is a curated library of 7 reusable templates (18 steps total across "Hosting switch," "Web design," "Game servers," "General outreach," "Follow-up") with `{{firstName}}`/`{{company}}` merge vars. But live campaigns store their own freeform copy in the `SequenceStep.bodyMarkdown` DB column (see `prisma/schema.prisma` `model SequenceStep`, editable at `/admin/coldemail/campaigns/[id]`) — a campaign can start from a template or be custom-written. The exact "quick one, Avenue Right" / "Worth a look before your next renewal?" text and the "Local Businesses — Shared Hosting (Variant A)" campaign name don't match anything in `templates.ts`, so that campaign was custom-authored, not pulled verbatim from the library. (Staging's DB has 0 `ColdCampaign` rows, so I couldn't inspect that live row directly — this is a code-based read.)

**Is adding a link simple? Yes — no technical or deliverability blocker.** `lib/coldemail/sender.ts`'s `markdownToHtml()` already supports `[label](https://...)` markdown links and bare autolinks. At send time, `buildMessage()` → `injectTracking()` automatically rewrites *every* `<a href="http...">` found in the body through the click-tracking redirect (it explicitly skips only the unsubscribe link, per RFC 8058). So inserting one link into a `bodyMarkdown` field is a one-line content edit; the platform does the wrapping for free. The `templates.ts` header comment itself states the design intent — "at most one link in the opener" — confirming links are expected, not avoided for deliverability. However, I grepped the entire curated library for `](` (markdown link syntax) and found **zero matches across all 7 templates / 18 steps** — the whole library currently ships link-free despite its own stated design intent. This looks like an oversight baked into the template library itself, not a one-off mistake on this campaign.

**Click tracking already exists**, fully separate from opens: `app/api/coldemail/track/click/[token]/route.ts` + `lib/coldemail/track.ts::recordClickEvent()` — HMAC-signed tokens (`clickTrackingToken` in `lib/coldemail/compliance.ts`) embed the destination URL so a tampered token 400s instead of becoming an open redirect. Each click writes an `EmailEvent(CLICK)`, bumps `ColdSend.clickCount`/`clickedAt`, and feeds `DeliverabilityEvent` for the analytics rollups in `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts`. This is production-ready and just waiting for a link to wrap.

**Best landing target:** `app/(marketing)/web-hosting/page.tsx` — the real, recently-redesigned shared-hosting page — is the natural fit for "Local Businesses — Shared Hosting." I found no dedicated cold-email-specific landing page or promo code for this segment (checked `lib/promotions.ts`, `lib/promo-redemption.ts`; no `COLDMAIL`/segment-tied promo exists). There's a generic `app/go/[slug]` short-link redirector in the codebase but nothing wired to cold email.

**Scope of the fix:** Not isolated — all 7 templates / 18 steps in `templates.ts` lack a link, so the same one-line fix (add a `[worth a look?](https://nxeon.cloud/web-hosting)`-style markdown link into each opener) should be applied library-wide, plus any already-customized live `SequenceStep.bodyMarkdown` rows per campaign (couldn't enumerate those — prod DB access wasn't available from this session).
